I am 55 years old and I have been farming for 30 years. I never went to school, so I don't read books or listen to those extension lectures — I learn by watching my neighbors and remembering what happened on my own fields. My household has only two people, me and my husband, so managing 20 mu is hard work. We switched to cabbage-cabbage-cabbage years ago because cabbage brings more cash than wheat and maize, and the vegetable buyers come right to the village to collect it. I used to grow wheat and maize when I was younger, but now I put all 20 mu into cabbage to get three harvests a year.

For the spring cabbage, I already planted the hybrid seeds I bought from the county supply store — I use "zhonggan 56" because it grows well here and the buyers recognize it. I rotary till the field first, then broadcast the compound fertilizer and plant. I put down about one big bag of compound fertilizer for every mu before planting, and when the heads start forming I topdress with urea. Cabbage needs a lot of water, so I irrigate five times from the well if the spring is dry. I spray for worms and diseases about six times because if the cabbage leaves get holes, the buyer pays almost nothing.

For the summer cabbage, I plant right after the spring harvest in June. The heat makes it harder, so I irrigate more — six times — and spray eight times because the insects are worse in summer. I use a heat-tolerant hybrid variety. The yield is usually a bit lower than spring because of the heat, around 7000 jin per mu.

For the autumn cabbage, this is my main money crop. I plant in August after the summer harvest and harvest in October. I put more fertilizer in because the soil is tired after two crops already. I expect about 8000 jin per mu if the weather is good. I irrigate five times and spray six times.

I hire women from the village for transplanting and harvest — about 15 days each season — because my back is not what it used to be and 20 mu is too much for two people alone. It costs money but without them the crop would rot in the field. I figure the seed, fertilizer, pesticide, and hired labor will cost a lot, but cabbage gives me cash three times a year, and that is what I need to buy food and medicine.
